From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Follow-up: deployment residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - recap + next steps

Hi Oliver,

Thanks again for the call this morning - great to hear more about NordBank's roadmap for AI assistants and the regulatory constraints you're balancing. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can scope an implementation that meets residency and compliance needs.

Recap / requirements I captured:
- Production customer data must remain in the EU (no cross-border persistence).
- Non-prod/dev data can be routed to Redwood-hosted regions outside the EU for testing, but would prefer EU staging where possible.
- You'd like clarity on hosted API (EU-only), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in EU), and Private (VPC or on-prem) trade-offs - esp. around control of logs, KMS, and audit trail retention.

High-level options:
1) Hosted API (EU-region only): fastest to launch. We can guarantee processing + data-at-rest inside EU regions (Frankfurt). Logs can be configured to retain in-region; full compliance evidence available (SOC 2).
2) Dedicated capacity (EU): reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and stronger isolation. Good middle ground when you need tenant isolation but want Redwood-managed infra.
3) Private VPC / on-prem: full customer-managed networking and KMS; required if you need air-gapped or on-prem data residency.

Next steps I propose:
- Please confirm whether the requirement is "all production data (including logs and model cache) must remain in the EU" vs "customer PII only; operational logs can be routed outside EU" - these two paths materially change the recommended deployment.
- I'll pull a quick matrix of region availability and recommended configuration (hosting vs dedicated vs private) - attaching a draft deployment_matrix.xlsx.
- If it looks useful, we can schedule a 30-min infra scoping call next week with your compliance/security folks and our solutions engineer (Marissa).

Attachments: deployment_matrix.xlsx (draft)

Would you be available Tue/Wed next week for the scoping call? Feel free to reply with preferred times or use my calendar: https://cal.com/lauren-bishop/30min

Best,

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - recap + next steps

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the clear recap - that matches our notes. To answer your question: for production, all customer data (including logs that could contain PII) must remain in the EU. Non-production (dev/test) can live outside EU for now, but we'd prefer EU staging where feasible.

A couple of clarifying questions before we schedule:
- For Hosted API: can you guarantee that neither request payloads nor KV/LLM cache are ever persisted outside the EU? We need that in writing for our procurement/compliance.
- For Private VPC/on-prem: do you have an on-prem deployment option that your team supports for initial rollout? If so, what are the typical lead times and minimum commitment?
- Do you have an initial security pack (SOC 2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration) we can share with our internal audit team? I attached our high-level security requirements (nordbank_security_req.pdf).

Also, can you provide a ballpark monthly estimate for a Dedicated EU deployment (throughput ~50 req/s, average 800 token responses) vs Hosted (pay-as-you-go) so we can flag budget to procurement?

If you need our security contact to join the scoping call: Ingrid Bergstrom <ingrid.bergstrom@nordbank.eu>.

Thanks,
Oliver
Head of Platform - Digital Banking
NordBank
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Apr 2028 08:30:00 +00:00
Subject: Fwd: NordBank residency questions - recommendations

Lauren / Marissa - forwarding Oliver's notes. Quick internal rec:

- If NordBank requires ALL production artifacts (payloads, logs, model cache) to reside in EU, our recommended paths are:
  * Dedicated (EU region) - fastest way to meet residency + isolation with Redwood-managed infra. Can offer reserved capacity, per-route SLAs, and we can configure logs to stay in-region. Good for predictable throughput.
  * Private VPC (EU) or On-prem - required if they need customer-managed networking or air-gapped solutions. This gives them full control of KMS and logging. Lead time depends on their infra team; typical pilot for Private VPC is ~6-8 weeks, on-prem 8-12+ weeks depending on access and compliance testing.

- Hosted API (EU-only) can be acceptable if they are comfortable with Redwood's in-region processing and our SOC 2 + contractual commitments around data residency. For strict bank requirements that demand customer-controlled keys or on-prem data flow, Private is the way.

- Pricing ask: I'll draft a rough estimate: Hosted (pay-as-you-go) pricing ranges based on token volume; Dedicated EU estimate for 50 req/s ~ $XXk-$YYk/month (we should produce a proper quote). I'll take point on a preliminary estimate pdf and MAP.

Next actions I recommend we own:
1) Send NordBank a short security pack (SOC 2 + KMS details) and a draft MAP + estimate.
2) Schedule infra scoping with their compliance and our solutions engineer (Marissa).
3) Confirm region specifics (we have Frankfurt eu-central-1 live; Paris eu-west-2 onboarding scheduled in Q3; APAC Tokyo available for APAC-specific deployments).

I'll prepare the estimate and MAP; Lauren, can you follow up with Oliver and lock the scoping call?

- Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
